newsitem.title: DENMARK: Sophus undecided on Rentokil move.
newsitem.headline: Sophus undecided on Rentokil move.

text.p: Danish holding company Sophus Berendsen, main shareholder in Britain's Rentokil, said on Wednesday that it had made no decision to place its 37.5 percent holding in Rentokil in a separately-listed company.
"A possible split is something that has intrigued the market for many years and the management is continously considering the idea," director Ole Balle told Reuters.
The group's share rose 5.7 percent to a record 865 crowns on Wednesday after a newspaper report that restructuring was imminent.
By 1120 GMT the share had fallen back to 836.52 crowns.
Rentokil contributed 533 million crowns to Sophus Berendsen's 640 million crown first-half 1996 earnings.

The group has sought to stress the earnings of its other holdings but last November admitted that losses in its Electronics and Data division meant that full-year non-Rentokil profits were likely to fall to 145 million crowns from 1995's 275 million.
